title: verify_padding reads a packet-controlled distance BELOW its chunk, into the block's earlier storage
live_proof: LIVE, read two-sided from the pinned tree. The negative-index read is present at v4.6.8:plugins/epan/opcua/opcua.c:332 -- 'if (padding[-pad_len + i] != pad_len) return -1;' -- verify_padding still has the single-argument signature at :324 ('static int verify_padding(const uint8_t *padding)'), and the fix's guard 'pad_len > available' has ZERO occurrences in the pinned file. The buffer is allocated at :642 with wmem_alloc(pinfo->pool, plaintext_len). pad_len is read from the packet ('pad_len = *padding'), so the distance below is attacker-chosen up to 255. NOTE: this defect was already triaged once and rejected ON SCOPE rather than on merit -- wireshark-wmem-defect-triage.md:147 calls it 'an out-of-bounds read inside a wmem_alloc'd buffer' and declined it because that file's scope was allocator lifetime.
object: the decrypted plaintext, plaintext_len bytes in the packet scope
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the object is alive throughout. Spatial row.
shape: packet-controlled negative index reads below the chunk, inside the same block
allocator_layer: block_fast -- the packet scope (pinfo->pool); the firing bound is wm_narrow()'s.
fidelity: model-consumer, real allocator. sig_len is reduced to 0 so the cursor is the chunk's last byte, and the loop is reduced to its first iteration (i = 0), the one that crosses. A predecessor chunk is allocated first and asserted below, because the class claim is that the crossing is a CHUNK bound: with no predecessor the same read would leave the block and be class A instead.
distinguishing: the only row in the corpus that crosses DOWNWARD. Class B while the chunk has a predecessor inside the block, degrading to class A when the chunk is first in a fresh block -- which a real capture may well produce, and this case does not establish either way.

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-06 on this host: the sequence COMPLETES, not caught. the platform's own bounds control fired in the same boot: cheribsd-bounds runs abi-probe oob, which sets bounds to exactly 16 and reads offset 16, and it PASSED alongside cheribsd-abi reporting CHERI_ABI pointer_bytes=16 runtime_revocation=1. A spatial completion is therefore a reading, not a silent detector. NOTE, corrected in the same edit: this arm previously said CHERI bounds the g_malloc'd block. On this harness there is no per-block malloc -- shared/driver.c hands the allocator ONE 384 MiB arena and src/native/regions.c carves it by bumping a cursor -- so the only CHERI bound in play is the arena. The completion is real; the reason is weaker than the arm used to claim. MEASURED 2026-10-07 WITH A REVOCATION CONTROL, results/20261007-cheribsd-revocation-control/: the sequence COMPLETES, NOT CAUGHT. 21 of 21 arms passed, runner exit 0, mode 0 (the port's unprotected baseline, which is the arm that asks what the shipping temporal mechanism does). The control FAULTED in the same boot -- tag_after_sweep=0 reissued=1, then SIGPROT si_code 2 at addr=pc=0x101dc0, equal to the probe address supervise resolved from the ELF independently -- so the revoker is shown to sweep and this completion means 'the mechanism is active and did not fire'. WHY A SECOND RUN: the 20260921-cheribsd bundle measured cases 0-12 at revocation on but contained NO revocation control, only a bounds control and a PoisonCap differential, neither of which shows the revoker sweeps; and it ran on image 3571a6d2..., a different vehicle. This run uses the image byte-identical to the ffmpeg and memcached readings, so the three programs' columns are comparable. The earlier bundle is kept for its PoisonCap arms.

native-detect.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-native-asan/: **NO ASan REPORT** on the buggy arm, which printed VERDICT DEFECT-REPRODUCED, so the defective access ran and ASan did not see it. The fixed arm exits 0 with VERDICT FIXED and no report. Built with the port's own allocator library under the same sanitizer (cc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0; -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g -O0; wmem and the port built with the same flags). Positive controls in the same run: `asan-control past 402653184` -> heap-buffer-overflow; `asan-control uaf 402653184` -> heap-use-after-free -- so ASan reports on a heap block the size of this corpus's arena, and the silence is the arena: one malloc'd block, carved and recycled without free(). Predicted before the run (b64cd18b85d0); the arm was previously 'declined'.
native-detect.note: DECLINED, not pending, and the reason is a measurement rather than an estimate: the two-sided shape is already established by the FFmpeg sub-object probe (ffmpeg/subobject-repros/results/20261005-native-subobject/asan-probe.c), where the member-to-member crossing draws NO report while a write one element past the whole allocation draws heap-buffer-overflow. Every crossing in this corpus stays inside one g_malloc'd block or slab page by the same mechanism, so eight more silent-with-control runs would confirm what one already showed. Two further reasons not to spend them: the wireshark corpus has no standalone native build to instrument, and the memcached one would have to instrument the case while linking an uninstrumented port library -- the mixed mode in which that probe's own -O1 artefact arose, where BOTH arms went silent because the dead stores were optimised away. If this arm is ever wanted, it needs its positive control in the same binary.
native-detect.prediction: NO ASan report: the crossing stays inside the one g_malloc'd block, so there is no redzone between the chunks to poison. A silent arm needs its own positive control -- a crossing past the END of the block, which ASan must report -- before it means anything.

native-fix-differential.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-native-differential/: the buggy sequence reaches storage outside its object (VERDICT DEFECT-REPRODUCED, exit 0) and the fixed sequence -- this case's upstream fix, modelled in case.c under wm_fixed -- does not (VERDICT FIXED, exit 0). Hosted build, upstream wmem allocator (WM_CHUNKS=OFF), `program 0 N buggy|fixed` (runners/run-native.sh). Spatial: the access address lies outside [object, object+size) in the buggy sequence and inside it, or is not made, in the fixed one. The arm did not exist before 2026-10-09: the cases had no fixed sequence.
